#project: # THE OPT-OUT for bashify's purge scorer, and the sibling of
# bin/lib/not-a-verb.tsv. Read by bashify/lib/closure.sh and by nothing else.
# Every row is a WRITTEN JUDGEMENT that a file NAMES a vendor or an agent
# without ever REACHING one, so its ESSENTIAL score is a measurement of its
# vocabulary rather than of its behaviour.
# THE RULE IT EXEMPTS FROM
#   surface_score_code() strips comment lines and counts what still matches
#   \b(claude|anthropic|openai|gpt|llm|assistant)|agent
#   Any hit makes the file ESSENTIAL, which bars it from a `bashified` branch.
# WHY AN EXEMPTION HAD TO EXIST. bashify/lib/surface.sh:54 predicted this and
# left the door unbuilt: "if one ever does it fails loudly and gets an
# exemption, which is the right way round for a guarantee of absence."
# Default-deny with an explicit, written escape is the correct shape and is not
# in dispute here -- what was missing was the escape.
# The case that forced it, 2026-08-11: realisateur's lints cannot be carried
# onto bashified, so the ten ~/.local/bin shims on every self-dev account keep
# a realisateur checkout load-bearing on eight accounts. They score ESSENTIAL
# highest-scoring line is:
#     echo "(offline-first: no claude calls -- findings are SIGNALS ...)"
# It fails a spend guard because it says it does not spend.
# WHAT A ROW IS NOT. It is not "this file is fine". It is a claim that EVERY
# match in that file is a path component, a filename, prose, or an inspection
# of something else's name -- and that the file invokes nothing. That claim is
# checkable in one command, and the row should say enough for a reader to
# check it:
#     grep -cE 'claude -p|claude --print|api\.anthropic' <file>     -> 0
# NEVER WIDEN THE REGEX INSTEAD. Broadening the pattern to spare these files
# would silently exempt a real spender somewhere nobody is looking. The value
# of the guard is that it is default-deny; the value of this file is that each
# escape is signed.
realisateur
